matches.factual_claim: Draft citation context: Rao and Layek, 2026, filler-control design, p. 3. Paragraph context: The closest 2026 work further narrows the opening. FaithLM already combines intervention-based evaluation with iterative explanation optimization. Rao and Layek then show why an answer-change effect needs specificity controls: unrelated filler or simply presenting the answer again can also change a later answer. REFLEX broadens refinement across tasks but explicitly leaves parts of the setting bounded. FaithLM, 2026, method, p. 4; Rao and Layek, 2026, filler-control design, p. 3; REFLEX, 2026, scope limitation, p. 15.
matches.evidence_quote: fluent, topic-unrelated filler text of matched length replaces the explanation

results.reason: The quotes establish that the audit used a matched-length, topic-unrelated filler condition, but they do not describe a re-injection control or report that either control produced answer changes. The statement’s conclusion therefore does not follow from the supplied quotes.

matches.title: What Does Answer Change Rate Actually Measure? A Specificity Audit of Causal Intervention Tests for Explanation Faithfulness
matches.factual_claim: Draft citation context: Rao and Layek, 2026, statistical limitation, p. 9. Paragraph context: Rao and Layek's 2026 audit is the closest methodological constraint. Their filler and re-injection controls show that an observed answer change is not automatically specific to explanation content. They do not claim or test statistical equivalence between controls, so our study will compare paired effect sizes with uncertainty rather than declaring controls equivalent after a nonsignificant test. Rao and Layek, 2026, statistical limitation, p. 9.
